**Status:** production invention; repository starter contract.

The configured production id is this starter's repository identity and temporary working title. The package delivers a deterministic film blocking pass, not a direct brief or reusable-only library. Its authored ladder ends in two six-second screenplay sources whose half-second dissolve produces an 11.5-second final timeline.

Required output consists of a deterministic preview, a deterministic feature, one pose guide pass, English accessibility captions, and a zero-gain audio mix whose only source is an inert structural pipeline fixture. Delivery ends after the terminal answer hold and its fade to black. A production whose complete intent fits one non-narrative observation instead selects `brief`; one that delivers reusable design and source without shots selects `library`.

Accessibility products for this single English, dialogue-free film are classified explicitly. The English caption track is required and is realized by the `starter-captions` deliverable and `film.tracks.captions`. No applicable product is optional or unsupported. Audio description is intentionally absent because this regression delivery limits itself to a visual blocking pass plus caption mapping; the consequence is that a recipient who cannot use the picture receives no equivalent account of the raised-hand and formation response. Subtitles, a synchronized transcript, sign-language rendition, and clean-audio alternatives are intentionally absent because the film has no second language, spoken dialogue, signed performance, or authored audible programme; the zero-gain guide is structural and is not an accessibility mix. The consequence is that recipients receive no alternate-language text, non-time-based transcript, signed presentation, or enhanced audible programme through those products. Accessible documentation and an operable alternative are outside this non-interactive timed-media delivery, and either becomes applicable only if delivery scope adds that product.

**Status:** production invention; repository starter contract.

The logline is: “A soloist raises a hand, and a chorus standing in rows answers it.” Every lower-layer tradeoff preserves one readable call-and-response: SOLOIST's raised hand is the call, CHORUS's ordered 2 m advance is the answer, and the held relation proves that answer was received. Detail that does not strengthen that observation or its deterministic verification is outside the starter.

**Status:** production invention; repository starter contract.

The audience receives only external audiovisual evidence selected by the screenplay and realized by reviewed shots: staged bodies, formation relations, the gate, the plaza, transitions, an accessibility caption, and deliberate silence. No private thought, narrator, dialogue, or off-screen causal fact is available. Cuts and dissolves may move between unequal-scale observations without implying that subjects moved between shots. The audience first sees an ambiguous raised-hand action, then may infer that it was an addressed cue only when the ordered formation visibly answers.

**Status:** production invention; repository starter contract.

English is the primary working language of authored production documents and the audience-facing accessibility caption. Exact code identifiers, numeric records, and standards terminology retain their declared forms. This starter authors no spoken or secondary language; adding one requires settings to define audience access and the screenplay to define its visible or audible content.

**Status:** production invention; repository convention.

All distances are metres and all durations are seconds. The world is right-handed with positive Y up, and `plaza-center` is the ground-level origin. Formation and model-local frames declare their relation to this shared frame instead of redefining it. These are chosen repository conventions, not measurements of an external place.

**Status:** derived; literal audit of the starter's declared delivery.

Backcasting the actual planned film consumers discovered explicit settings owners in `000-governing-aim.md`, `010-soloist.md`, `020-chorus.md`, `030-gate.md`, `040-plaza.md`, and `050-art-direction.md`. They own the production identity, delivery, aim, recipient access, language, units, time, SOLOIST, CHORUS, GATE, PLAZA, capabilities, relations, initial states, limits, visual and audible grammar, and delivery observations the current model, motion, narrative, shot, and film-source work actually consumes.

The visible-subject and design breakdown is exhaustive for this film: SOLOIST routes to `010-soloist.md`, CHORUS to `020-chorus.md`, GATE to `030-gate.md`, PLAZA to `040-plaza.md`, and the far-haze effect to `050-art-direction.md`. Each is built by reviewed project source; no external asset or generated rendition is adopted. The only reused item is the inert pipeline fixture, which carries no visible subject or appearance. No subject, design, or appearance remains unowned or deferred.

Ordinary daylight and gravity are incidental defaults under `obligations/core/settings.md#minimal-departure` because no consequential dependency in this delivery requires a more specific owner. Human scale is explicit canon under `050-art-direction.md#art-scale`. No material settings requirement found by the current discovery and consumer backcast is outside scope or unresolved. If a production-contract or downstream-consumer change discovers another material requirement, its consumer remains blocked until the map records a current H2 owner, justified incidental default, delivery-scope boundary, or decision condition and research path.
